newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The coach of the Melbourne Australian Football League team, Neil Balme, could be under pressure to hold his job when the Demons board meets today. The Melbourne Demons are at the bottom of the AFL ladder after five straight losses, and president Joe Gutnik gave a strong indication that changes were imminent. Page 25.

Australian Olympian, Ian Brown, will be named head coach of the Australian Yachting Federation for the 2000 Olympics campaign today. Brown will start work after beating a field of local and foreign contenders for the position. Page 26.

Australian tennis player, Jason Stoltenberg, defeated Swede, Magnus Norman, 6-4 5-7 6-3 to reach the final of the AT&T Challenge against Marcelo Filippini of Uruguay. Leading up to the semi-finals clash, Stoltenberg is ranked seventh-seed, while Filippini remains at 92 in the world. Page 30.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

North Sydney lock Gary Larson was cited last night for an alleged spear tackle on Western Suburbs winger Aseri Laing. Larson will now join Illawarra's Trent Barrett to face the Australian Rugby League judiciary tonight. Barrett was sent off for a high tackle during yesterday's draw with Manly. Page 27.

Assurances that Matt Williams will remain coach of the New South Wales rugby union team are in question after an influential Waratah official made private inquiries as to whether a successful high-profile coach will be available to take over next season. The NSW Rugby Union has publicly backed Williams, and no official approach to the other coach has been made. Page 29.

The Australian women's hockey team, the Hockeyroos, defeated China 5-0 after China arrived three hours late for the Melbourne match yesterday. Women's Hockey Australia officials were disappointed with the delay which disrupted flight plans, gate-takings, team preparation, and other games. Page 31.
THE AGE

Sydney Swans' Wade Chapman was taken to hospital for observation last night after a collision with Carlton's Matthew Hogg during their AFL match at the Sydney Cricket Ground. Sydney's coach, Rodney Eade, said Chapman had severe concussion, and could miss two games. Page S3.

Australian golfer Craig Parry fell from equal second place to joint sixth in the Houston Open yesterday. Parry started the third day one shot off the lead but fell to four shots behind after a one-over-par 73. Page S17.

Australian golfer, Karrie Webb, hit a three-under-par round of 69 in the Sprint Titleholders Championship in Florida yesterday, placing her at eight-under, six strokes behind leader Kris Tschetter who joined twelve other players who could not compete the round due to a lightning storm. Page S17.
THE HERALD SUN

New Zealand driver, Greg Murphy, is back in contention for the Australian Touring Car Championship after winning two of the three heats at a wet Symmons Plains race track yesterday. It was the Holden Racing Team driver's first touring car championship road victory. Page 94.

Adelaide City beat Marconi 4-0 to secure a semi-final place in soccer's Ericsson Cup yesterday. Adelaide City will play the minor semi-final against South Melbourne, who defeated the Melbourne Knights 3-0 yesterday. Page 89.

The mare Saleous, the winner of the 1995 VRC Oaks and Wakeful Stakes, was put down yesterday after failing to recover from foot surgery. Saleous was the mare that put ex-champion jockey Pat Hyland in the big leagues as a trainer. Page 87.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian long-distance swimmer, Susie Maroney, is likely to begin her attempt to swim from Cuba to the United States on Thursday, a day later than scheduled, due to poor weather in the Florida Straits. It was poor weather conditions that forced Maroney to abandon her 1996 attempt at the swim 10 kilometres from land. Page 50.

Illawarra survived a frantic final seven minutes with only 11 players to hold last year's premiers Manly to a 34-34 draw at WIN Stadium yesterday. The scoreline equalled the highest draw in the Australian Rugby League competition set by Norths and Parramata in 1949. Page 33.

Rugby league player, Clinton Schifcofske, was back playing for the South Queensland Crushers in the ARL competition yesterday, only a few weeks after testing positive to steroids. Although the winger kicked three goals, his comeback effort was not enough the Crushers lost to St George 32-22. Page 40.
